answer: The opal counter is kept in forge and juniper makes public each reset. An adversary thus has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 20 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 20 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 25 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
